For a wide row \(j\in B_{\rm w}\) let \(S_j=\bigcup_{T\ni j}C(p_{T,j})\) be the union of the cubes of its patterns over the terms on it; the wide graph \(G\) of the wide-rounds entry has the edges \((j,x)\), \(j\in R'\cap B_{\rm w}\), \(x\in Q\cap S_j\). For a label \(x\) let the row degree \(d_{\rm r}(x)=|\{j\in B_{\rm w}:\ x\in S_j\}|\) and the row mass \(m_{\rm r}=\sum_xd_{\rm r}(x)=\sum_j|S_j|\); \(d_{\rm r}\le d_{\rm w}\) and \(m_{\rm r}\le m_{\rm w}\), with equality when no two patterns on a row overlap. Lemma W2 (rows). Lemma W2 and its polynomial form hold with \(d_{\rm r}\), \(\mathrm{Heavy}=\{x:\ d_{\rm r}(x)>D\}\) and \(m_{\rm r}\) in place of \(d_{\rm w}\), \(\mathrm{Heavy}\) and \(m_{\rm w}\). Proof. The recorded proof uses the wide degree once, to bound the number of rows adjacent to a hole \(x_i\) of a matching; that number is \(d_{\rm r}(x_i)\). \(\square\)

The theorem has no hypothesis on the number of terms, the widths, the number of patterns per row or the number of rows, and its failure is per reader; a source of \(n^c\) such readers costs \(n^c\) times \(2n^{-c-1}\). It contains the pin-free reader \(F_p\) of the shared-cube lemma at every size: its row mass \(2|B|\) is below \(4N(n+1)\), its heavy holes are the two labels of \(C(p)\), and case (D2) gives at most two hole queries, as the census of the wide-rounds entry showed. It contains the unary readers, the terms \([j=z]\) of width \(\ell\), on the wide-round tree, where the recorded unary theorem used its own hole-query trees; and it contains the reader with every pattern of \(\ell-1\) literals on every row of \(B\), of row mass \(n|B|\), which case (D1) satisfies at the root except with probability \(e^{-N}\) when \(|B|\ge4N+1\) and case (D2) covers otherwise; that reader has a term satisfied at the root as soon as some row of \(B\) is matched, its \(S_j\) being the whole label set (Section 5). It is not implied by an earlier result: Corollary 1 of the wide-rounds entry needs the wide mass condition, which fails for this family from size \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) on; Corollary A of the previous entry needs few rows; the dichotomy does not apply to pin-free terms of width above \(\ell-\ell_2-1\); and the recorded unary theorem's height grows with the source size. Case (D1) needs no hypothesis on \(N\) beyond \(N\ge1\), and case (D2) is Lemma W2; the split at \(4N(n+1)\) is where the two meet, and \(\varepsilon<\tfrac12\) serves only to make \(4N(N+1)(n+1)\le n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) satisfiable for large \(n\).

The frontier block is a wide disjunction of narrow terms, each the conjunction of at most \(r_{\rm high}\) affine conditions ( frontier ). In the bit encoding a form is a sum over rows of an affine functional of the row's label, \(L=\sum_j\lambda_j(\text{label}_j)\). A literal condition is a form supported on one row. Conjecture L, proved in full, would give an old-only image for exactly those readers whose terms consist of one-row conditions. For proof systems this is the situation of bounded-depth Frege without counting gates, where PHP lower bounds are classical (cited as context in cycle 174, not used). It is not sufficient for \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege: no proved source restriction excludes low blocks on forms with large row support, the low-block decision shows that restriction does not remove them, and a restriction \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) turns such a form into the form \(\sum_{j\in R'}\lambda_j|_Q+\beta\), \(\beta=\sum_{j\notin R'}\lambda_j(\mu'(j))\), which still involves every residual row on which \(\lambda_j\) is not constant on \(Q\); a form supported on at least half the rows has at least \((N+1)/4\) residual rows except with probability \(e^{-\Omega(N)}\), and a given linear part is constant on \(Q\) with probability about \(1/N\) (simultaneously for all rows that share it), so with probability \(1-O(1/N)\) the restricted form involves a constant fraction of the residual rows, above the height budget; this is far from the failure \(O(n^{-c-1})\) that switching needs. This is the recorded statement that terms containing parities do not switch. Nor is the literal machinery known to be necessary: a mechanism for dense forms would contain the literal case, but nothing recorded indicates that it would take the form of the pinned trees, rounds and covers built in cycles 175 to 214.

Symmetric forms. If every form of the reader has the same functional on every row, \(a_j=a\), then by (DF-restrict) and \(\sum_{x\notin Q}x=0\) for \(\ell_2\ge2\), \(L|_{\rho'}=\langle B^{\mathsf T}a,Y\rangle+\langle a,q_0\rangle+c\) with \(Y=\sum_{j\in R'}y_j\), because \(N+1\) is odd. The whole reader is a function of \(Y\in\mathbb F_2^{\ell_2}\): \(m\le\ell_2=\log_2N\), and Lemma P gives an exact image with \(s=\log_2N+w\), for every \(\rho'\) and any number of terms. More generally, forms that are symmetric within each of \(g\) classes of rows have \(m\le\ell_2\min(g,N+1)\); before any restriction such a reader is already a function of \(g\ell\) forms and Lemma P packs it without a restriction at \(s=g\ell+w\), polylogarithmic for polylogarithmic \(g\), although it may sit in the syntactic frontier zone; so the symmetric case shows no gain of the restriction either. Sparse forms reduce to conditions on boundedly many residual rows (alternative (B) of the review ). The first falsification target of Question D therefore fails to defeat anything: symmetric and class-symmetric forms are the easy case, not a hard one.

Hence the coverage hypothesis of Question D is false at the balanced rank \(w\approx\log_2a\), which lies inside the frontier zone (ranks below \(r_{\rm high}\), more than polylogarithmically many terms): there, for each fixed \(\rho'\), the restricted reader is a nonconstant function on \(V\) with both values on a constant share of the points except with probability \(2^{-v/3+2}\) over the source, so by Markov's inequality, for all but a \(2^{-v/6+1}\) fraction of sources this holds for all but a \(2^{-v/6+1}\) fraction of the restrictions; and by Lemma I the restricted reader is distributed exactly as a random reader of the same shape on a cube of dimension \(v\). The restriction replaces the dimension \((n+1)\ell\) by \(v\) and changes nothing else: the balanced rank is untouched by it. No tree or image within the budget is known for such a reader. Each restricted form involves every residual row with a nonzero \(B^{\mathsf T}a_j\), all but about one of the \(N+1\) rows on average; an exact image certified by Booleanity alone must equal \(P\) on \(V\), so its degree is the \(\mathbb F_2\)-degree of the complement of a random union of about \(2^w\) flats, for which no bound is proved here; and the universal source-map obstruction , which concerns its own three-level source, names certificates from genuine PHP consequences as the escape. For generic sources of size \(n^c\) the ranks therefore split as follows.

Board: \(N+1\) rows, \(N\) holes, cell variables over \(\mathbb F_2\). System A has Booleanity, the row exclusions and the row axioms \(Q_j=\sum_xX_{jx}-1\); its models are the labelings. System B adds the hole exclusions and is the functional PHP of the image lemma . \(T_d\) is the span of the monomials of degree at most \(d\) that survive the exclusions: partial labelings for A, partial matchings for B. \(V_d\subseteq T_d\) is the degree-\(d\) polynomial-calculus closure of the row axioms: the span of \(tQ_j\), \(|t|\le d-1\), closed under multiplying elements of degree at most \(d-1\) by variables, the low-degree elements being read off an echelon basis whose pivots prefer high degree. For system A the quotient dimensions equal \(\sum_{k\le d}\binom{N+1}k(N-1)^k\), the functions of row-degree at most \(d\), in every case computed (16, 106, 376 for \(N=4\)), which validates the closure. In every nonvacuous case the closure equals the span of the \(tQ_j\); the closure rounds add elements only at the refutation degree (\(N=4\), \(d=3\): 325 to 381, all of \(T_3\)).

Rank-two inputs at the balanced rank (eight holes, \(s=w=2\), hole axioms, \(V_4\)): six readers with \(a=2,4,8\) independent terms \(t_k=(1+L_k)(1+L'_k)\) on dense forms with uniform half-sets, two readers for each \(a\); \(a=2^w\) is the analogue, at the smallest scale, of the balanced rank of the previous entry , and \(a=2,8\) lie on either side of it. Unknowns are \(\hat P\in T_2\) and constants \(U_k\); the conditions are \(1-\hat P-\sum_kU_kt_k\in V_2\) and \(t_k\hat P\in V_4\). All six readers are infeasible with the hole axioms. Without them an image must equal \(P\) on labelings, and for all six a nonzero three-row mixed difference of \(P\) shows row-degree at least three, so they are infeasible there as well. The control with \(t_1=[x_0=0](1+L)\), \(t_2=[x_1=0](1+L')\), where \(t_1t_2\) vanishes by a hole exclusion and \(\hat P=1+t_1+t_2\), is feasible with the hole axioms and excluded without them by the same mixed-difference test.

The test has low power, and the limits matter more than the result. Position of the general step. In these terms the notebook's source is a system of extension variables of constant nesting depth, polynomial in number, whose defining polynomials depend on all original variables. The published bounds stop at arity \(N^{1-\varepsilon}\) with a tradeoff against the number of extension variables, and both papers say explicitly that extension variables depend on original variables only; the first identifies the recursive case with \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege, which is the mapping used here. That boundary is the one the notebook found from its own side: forms of row support at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/(N+1)\) reduce to boundedly many residual rows under the compact restriction (alternative (B) of the route review ), an analogue of a restriction shrinking an extension axiom of arity \(N^{1-\varepsilon}\) (there the reduction goes through the XOR gadget of the lifted formula and the size bound of the axiom, here through sparse row support, so the mechanisms are analogous and not the same), while for dense forms the restriction changes nothing at the balanced rank ( Lemmas I and B ). The remark on \(p=2\) reduces their question to the degree of the augmented system only in their parameter range, fewer than about \(n^2/\kappa^2\) extension variables; for the polynomially many dense extension variables of a compiled source the size-degree tradeoff is void. The notebook's general step is also a degree statement for the augmented system, but for a different reason (a contradiction below the old degree barrier for a compiled source, with the inventory entering through the weight). Their factor-\(\kappa\) bound is the analogue of the recorded substitution cost, which is additive in the rank at one level and multiplicative along chains; both are void for dense inputs. The caveat of the second paper bears on the form of the step: a method that handled arbitrary nested dense extension variables would prove more than the main goal, so the step should use the block format of the compiled source, in agreement with the universal obstruction and with the route item as stated. So the obligation is not covered by a known technique with different parameters; it sits beyond the published frontier in the dense and nested direction. One difference in method is worth keeping: both papers restrict the original variables so as to simplify the extension axioms and then repair the hard formula, whereas the notebook restricts to a residual PHP and asks the source to have an image there; their cleanup step, which restores a hard sub-instance after each restriction, has no counterpart in the notebook, and their hard formula (the generalized PHP, which maps \(r\)-subsets of pigeons and tolerates such cleanups) is not the ordinary PHP of the main goal.

One difference in method is worth keeping: both papers restrict the original variables so as to simplify the extension axioms and then repair the hard formula, whereas the notebook restricts to a residual PHP and asks the source to have an image there; their cleanup step, which restores a hard sub-instance after each restriction, has no counterpart in the notebook, and their hard formula (the generalized PHP, which maps \(r\)-subsets of pigeons and tolerates such cleanups) is not the ordinary PHP of the main goal.
This is a restatement, not a new lemma: the normal form removes a block whose literal input span contains one, and the step applies it to the images of the inputs instead of the literal inputs.

Survivors. For a generic reader of \(a=n^c\) terms of rank \(w\) on the residual bit space of dimension \(v\), the step applies for \(w\le w_1\approx c\log_2n/\log_2(2v+2)\) and the weight clamps the terms for \(w\ge r_{\rm high}\). The expected number of uncovered points is \(2^v(1-2^{-w})^a\), so the covering threshold is \(a\ln(1/(1-2^{-w}))=v\ln2\) (for \(w=1\) this is \(a=v\); for large \(w\) it is \(a2^{-w}\approx v\ln2\)). Two zones survive. Between \(w_1\) and the threshold the reader is constant with high probability, but only a covering certificate with constant coefficients is excluded and the cost of a certificate with polynomial coefficients is open (the second row of the table of the dense-forms entry ). Beyond the threshold, with a margin (by the variance bound of Lemma B the probability of no uncovered point is at most the reciprocal of the mean), the reader is not constant as a function; this zone contains the balanced rank. In both zones exact packing costs about \(aw\), and the count of cycle 174, which is what produces a weight, needs \(k\ge v\ln(16a)/w\) for a weight of degree \(k\) vanishing on all \(a\) flats, more than \(0.69\,v\) at the balanced rank against \(k\le v/4\) (that no weight exists is expected for generic flats but is not proved, here or in cycle 174). These survivors are the frontier recorded in cycles 173 and 174. A block reading a surviving reader has no input image to which the step could apply, so the induction stops at its first step for every source that contains one such reader, and the question of dependence between levels is not reached. The proposal of the previous entry is withdrawn as a route: it handles a generic source only if the source has no reader in these zones.

Reduction. Call a source pure over \(T\) if it consists of the blocks of \(T\) and of higher blocks each of whose inputs is an \(\mathbb F_2\)-affine combination of earlier products, with no old variables, no raw coefficients and no products of products. If \(\mathcal F\cup\{Z_c+e_c:c\in T\}\) has no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree \(B\), then no source pure over \(T\) has a refutation of degree \(B/\max(1,w-1)\). Any accuracy is allowed. The statement uses of the base only its Boolean equations and of \(T\) only the exactness of the flat indicators; it extends the recorded constant-value profiles of eligible zero clamps ( zero-value profile , shared core ) from zero clamps supplied by the weight to arbitrary constants under a hardness hypothesis. Proof: the telescoping substitution gives each block of \(T\) the product image \(Z_c\) with coefficient images of degree at most \(w-1\). A reader of products of \(T\) has inputs congruent to constants modulo the added axioms. If some input \(g\) is congruent to 1, the first coefficient row that selects this input alone gives the product image \(1+g\), a constant combination of the added axioms, hence congruent to 0, and every companion image is a multiple of it. If all inputs are congruent to 0, the zero coefficient rows give the product image 1, and each companion image is an input, again a combination of the added axioms. Either way the reader's product is congruent to a constant, and the same argument applies one level up. The images of the axioms of the source have certificates within \(\max(1,w-1)\) times their original degrees (companions of \(T\): \(w+1\) against \(3(w-1)\) for \(w\ge2\); field equations: \(2(w-1)\); reader companions: at most \(2w\) against \(5(w-1)\)). Every line of a refutation of the source maps to a consequence of the enlarged base of degree at most \(\max(1,w-1)\) times its own. \(\square\) (A reader that also has a nonconstant affine part becomes a first-level block of the quotient and joins \(T\) with its own value; this case is not needed below.)

Lemma S (the recorded case split, in polynomial-calculus form). The Nullstellensatz form over every \(\mathbb F_p\), with loss \((p-1)s\) for a query of degree \(s\), its contrapositive and its iteration along a query tree are recorded in the case-split budget ; the polynomial-calculus proof and the phrasing for term values are the only additions. Let \(Z\) be an old polynomial of degree \(w\le B\) with \(Z^2-Z\) in the Boolean ideal through \(2w\). If \(\mathcal F\cup\{Z\}\) and \(\mathcal F\cup\{1+Z\}\) both have refutations of degree \(B\), then \(\mathcal F\) has one of degree \(B+w\). Proof: multiply every line of the first refutation by \(1+Z\) and of the second by \(Z\). The axiom \(Z\) becomes \(Z(1+Z)\), a Boolean consequence through \(2w\le B+w\); the old axioms and the rules stay within \(B+w\). The two derivations end at \(1+Z\) and \(Z\), whose sum is 1. \(\square\)

Alternatives. (A) Question H for parity constraints: the polynomial-calculus degree of the compact base on a generic affine subspace of codimension up to \(0.7v\). The hardness part of Claim G now has three levels: axioms confining all labels to one flat (recorded), axioms confining each row to its own flat, which is a PHP on a bipartite graph and should be covered by published expansion bounds (not read), and generic row-mixing equations (open). The last is the single statement on which both the generic model and the test of Section 4 depend, it is sharp (a refutation strategy of low degree would end the value method for dense terms), and cheap exact experiments exist. (B) The dual target, the parked level-one conjecture . Cycle 173 already judged that it does not move the obligation, and nothing since has changed that. (C) Mixed terms and the simultaneous choice of \(E\) for structured sources. Premature: without part (i) for the simplest axioms there is nothing to combine. (D) The alternatives of the earlier reviews (active-window reduction, density coordinates, PHP-relative interfaces, virtual clause source); their placement is unchanged. (E) Extending the published methods for polynomial calculus with extension variables (quadratic degree, restrictions with cleanup) towards dense arity. Not selected now: both papers need a formula that survives their cleanup restrictions (an XOR lift of a generalised PHP in one, selector variables over a family whose large subsets stay hard in the other), and the PHP of the main goal is not of that kind; it stays the fallback if (A) fails, because a failure of (A) would say that hardness under generic linear constraints is the wrong invariant and that size-based measures should be looked at.

The two lines of the last weeks are its extreme cases. For literal terms \(E\) is a matching restriction of the compact family, (i) is the preservation of the compact base, and (ii) is switching ( Conjecture L ). For generic dense terms in a pure source \(E\) consists of term values, (ii) is trivial by the reduction of the last entry, and (i) is Question H. The recorded structure of the base fits the same language: the compact bit base is itself a system of \(\binom{n+1}2\) avoidance axioms for flats of codimension \(\ell\), the collision flats \(\{\mathrm{label}_i=\mathrm{label}_{i'}\}\), of total density about \(n/2\), which is below the generic covering threshold \(v\ln2\) of the last entry although the structured flats do cover the space. Part (i) asks that further avoidance axioms or linear equations, generic or chosen from a proof, leave this system hard.

The goal needs Claim G for every source compiled from a small proof, with \(B\) and \(s\) polylogarithmic and the factors multiplied along a fixed number of levels. The line has not touched three parts of this. First, (i) has a recorded proof only for structured \(E\): axioms that confine every label to one flat, or that fix rows by a matching, leave a compact base with fewer holes, which is hard by the recorded decoder and bridge (Section 4). For generic \(E\) the notebook has no technique: the weight gives hardness only for avoiding flats above the high threshold, restrictions do not act on dense forms, the case split loses total rank, and a complete affine block never imposes a value. Second, different parts of one source may need incompatible axioms, as in the union above, and mixed terms, with a literal part and a dense part, need both kinds at once; no statement for either exists. Third, the choice of \(E\) must work for all readers of a source simultaneously; for generic terms this is automatic, for structured terms it is a combinatorial problem that has not been posed. What the line does supply is a formulation in which the universal obstruction does not apply, since images are certified relative to the enlarged base and not on the Boolean cube; Section 4 checks this on the obstruction's own source.

The original coordinates, and twists row by row. Here Claim G holds in full with recorded hardness (the reviewer's observation, checked against the records). Let \(J\) consist of the same \(\ell'=\lfloor0.3\ell\rfloor\) bit positions of every label, fixed before the circuit is sampled, and let \(E\) set all other bit positions of every label to zero. By the count below, which applies to any fixed set of at most \(0.3v\) coordinates, every term of a suitable circuit contains a zeroed bit, so (ii) holds with constant images. The fixed positions contribute the factor 1 to every collision polynomial, so the base with \(E\) adjoined is the compact bit base of \(n+1\) rows and \(2^{\ell'}\) holes. It has no refutation through \(2^{\ell'}/2\), about \(n^{0.3}/2\): the decoder transfer holds for every number of rows and every ceiling when \(\ell'\ge2\), and the imported bound for the functional PHP holds whenever there are more rows than holes. The same is true for a twist that applies one affine bijection of \(\mathbb F_2^\ell\) to every label, since the base is invariant under relabelling the holes. So the recorded obstruction source does not resist value axioms; this is the escape that the obstruction entry itself names, a justified restriction that preserves a sufficient old barrier, with the indicator of the subspace, a weight of degree about \(0.7v\), replaced by adjoined axioms and a hardness statement. What is open is exactly a twist that mixes rows.

Proof (the reviewer's derivation, checked against the records). Let \(R=\prod_{i\in I}(1+L_i)\), the indicator of the solution space, of degree \(a\). Its monomial \(\prod_ib_{i,j_i}\) has coefficient one, because no \(w_{i'}\) contains a pivot, and it uses one bit in each of \(a\) distinct rows. Suppose \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\cup\tau\Phi\) has a refutation of degree \(B\); a refutation of \(\mathcal Q\cup\Phi\) gives one by the decoder transfer , since the images \(\tau L_i\) are axioms of the target. Multiply every line by the weight \(\tau R\), using the recorded weighted replay . An old axiom \(g\) costs \(\deg g+a\). For the axiom \(\lambda=\tau L_i\) the weighted line is \(\tau\bigl(\prod_{i'\ne i}(1+L_{i'})\bigr)(\lambda^2+\lambda)\), and in characteristic two \(\lambda^2+\lambda=\sum_e(x_e^2-x_e)\) over the cells of \(\lambda\), a Boolean consequence of degree two; the cost is \(a+1\le B+a\). So \(\tau R\in\mathcal C_{B+a}(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun})\). By the recorded top-monomial detector , with \(u=a\) and ceiling \(B+a\), this is impossible when \(4(a-1)<n\) and \(n\ge2(B+a)-1\). Hence \(2(B+a)-1>n\), that is \(B\ge n/2-a+1\). \(\square\)

For the axiom \(\lambda=\tau L_i\) the weighted line is \(\tau\bigl(\prod_{i'\ne i}(1+L_{i'})\bigr)(\lambda^2+\lambda)\), and in characteristic two \(\lambda^2+\lambda=\sum_e(x_e^2-x_e)\) over the cells of \(\lambda\), a Boolean consequence of degree two; the cost is \(a+1\le B+a\). So \(\tau R\in\mathcal C_{B+a}(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun})\). By the recorded top-monomial detector , with \(u=a\) and ceiling \(B+a\), this is impossible when \(4(a-1)<n\) and \(n\ge2(B+a)-1\). Hence \(2(B+a)-1>n\), that is \(B\ge n/2-a+1\). \(\square\)

This is the weight step of the one-affine-level theorem with the weight equal to the indicator of the subspace, which is affordable exactly because the rank is small. In the language of the literature: \(\Phi\) is safe if and only if the top-degree part of that indicator contains a monomial with one bit in each of \(a\) rows (the coefficient of a squarefree monomial of degree \(a\) is the corresponding minor, which is the criterion of their Theorem 3.1), and the detector's disjoint coordinate edges are the pairs of holes of Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson.

A direct restriction shows what is left of the PHP. Choose labels \(h_i\), \(i\in I\), one after another so that the \(2a\) labels \(h_i^0,h_i^1\) (the two ends of the edge through \(h_i\) in direction \(j_i\), with pivot bit 0 and 1) are distinct, which is possible because before the \(i\)-th choice at most \(2(i-1)<n/2\) of the \(n/2\) edges of direction \(j_i\) are blocked. In unary variables send \(x_{i,h_i^1}\mapsto u_i\), \(x_{i,h_i^0}\mapsto1+u_i\) and the other cells of row \(i\) to zero, where \(u_i\) is \(\tau(w_i+c_i)\) with \(\tau(b_{i',t})\) replaced by the constant \((h_{i'})_t\) for every \(i'\in I\), the row \(i\) itself included, at \(t\ne j_{i'}\) (both ends of an edge agree there, so this is what the map gives), and with the reserved cells of the other rows set to zero; and send \(x_{k,h}\mapsto0\) for every row \(k\notin I\) and every reserved label \(h\). The row axioms of \(I\) go to zero, Booleanity and same-row products of \(I\) to \(u_i^2+u_i\) of degree two, the column exclusions that involve a row of \(I\) to zero by disjointness of the pairs, and \(\tau L_i\) to zero; what remains is exactly the functional PHP with \(n+1-a\) rows and \(n-2a\) holes, at ceiling \(\max(B,2)\). The imported bound for more rows than holes gives the same \(n/2-a+1\). (The reviewer checked every image of this map; the first draft carried out the same restriction in the bit variables, which needed the label-decoder certificate and an extra hypothesis \(n-2a>2\ell\) that the unary form does not need.)

Several pivots in one row. If the reduced system has pivot sets \(T_i\) in \(u\) rows, \(a=\sum_i|T_i|\), the indicator has the squarefree top monomial \(\prod_i\prod_{t\in T_i}b_{it}\), and the recorded multi-axis cube detector applies with ceiling \(B+a\) whenever pairwise disjoint coordinate cubes with free axes \(T_i\) exist ( packing ): with \(F=\sum_i2^{|T_i|}\) reserved labels, every refutation has degree at least \((n-F)/2-(a-u)+1\) (the lemma's other hypotheses, \(m\ge B+a\) and a residual label, are harmless: if they fail, \(B\) already exceeds the stated bound or the bound is at most one). Since \(2^p\ge2p\), one has \(F\ge2a\), so \(F\le n/2\) gives \(a\le n/4\) exactly, and a nonvoid bound needs \(a<n/2\) in any case: several pivots in a row never buy more rank than single pivots.

What the corollary is worth. Its loss, one degree per equation, equals that of the recorded case split ; the gain over the case split is that it holds for every right-hand side and every safe system, not for some sign vector. It does not reach what the value method needs: the row-mixing twist of the review needs rank about \(0.7v\), far above the number of blocks, where no system is safe, the cubes cannot be packed, and any bound of the form \(n/2-a\) is void.

Design. The tool of the previous finite check , parity constraints in the affine family (forms linear in the label bits, which correspond to linear equations on the compact base through the decoder), now also on sixteen holes at degree two: 17 rows, \(v=68\), 32913 monomials, refutation degree at least nine, three seeds, with the bijective and labelings controls. Sixteen holes at degree three (about 2.3 million monomials) is out of reach of the tool.

Proof. The coordinate-completion lemma gives an affine equivalence \(E\) of \(\mathbb F_2^v\) with \((E(b))_{e(c)}=\Lambda_c(b)\) and a parametrization \(P_0=E^{-1}\circ z\) of \(W\) by the free coordinates; any other injective affine \(P\) with image \(W\) is \(P_0\circ A\) for an affine bijection \(A\) of \(\mathbb F_2^k\), so \(P\) has an affine left inverse \(\lambda:\mathbb F_2^v\to\mathbb F_2^k\) (take \(A^{-1}\) of the free coordinates of \(E\)), and \(P(\lambda(b))=b+\sum_c\Lambda_c(b)\,h_c\) for fixed vectors \(h_c\in\mathbb F_2^v\): in the coordinates of \(E\) the map \(P\circ\lambda\) sets the designated coordinates to zero and keeps the others.

First inequality: apply the substitution replay with \(T=1\), \(w=1\) to \(b\mapsto P(y)\), at the ceiling \(D_b\). A Boolean axiom \(b^2+b\) goes to \(g^2+g\) for an affine form \(g=\sum_jg_jy_j+g_0\), which over \(\mathbb F_2\) equals \(\sum_jg_j(y_j^2+y_j)\), a combination of Boolean axioms of degree two (the cross terms cancel in characteristic two; this is the certificate used in the decoder ). Each \(\Lambda_c\circ P\) is an affine polynomial that vanishes on all of \(\mathbb F_2^k\), hence the zero polynomial. Each \(E_{ii'}\) goes to an axiom of \(\mathcal S_P\). So every axiom image is derived within the ceiling and \(\mathcal S_P\) is refuted within \(D_b\).

Lower bound \(\ell\): \(\Lambda\cup{\rm BOOL}_b\) has the common zeros \(W\ne\varnothing\), so a refutation uses a collision axiom, a line of degree \(\ell\). Quotient ring: reduce an ordinary proof line by line as in the functional bridge (an ordinary multiplication with nonzero predecessor has \(\deg P+1\le D\), so the quotient inference has the same charge); conversely a quotient inference \(P\mapsto\overline{y_jP}\) is the ordinary product \(y_jP\) of degree \(\deg P+1\) minus multiples \(m'(y_j^2+y_j)\) of the same degree. The quotient-ring axiom is the multilinear reduction of \(E_{ii'}\circ P\), of degree \(e_{ii'}\), while the ordinary product can have degree up to \(\ell\) when its forms are dependent; passing between the two costs at most \(\ell\), inside the ceiling, so \(D_y^{\rm quot}\le D_y^{\rm ord}\le D_b\le\max(D_y^{\rm quot},\ell)\). \(\square\)

So the PHP on \(W\) is, exactly and in bit degree, the statement that the \(\binom{n+1}2\) collision flats of the \(n+1\) affine maps \(P_i:\mathbb F_2^k\to\mathbb F_2^\ell\) cover \(\mathbb F_2^k\). For a uniform \(W\) the maps are generic, the flats have codimension \(\ell\) once \(k\ge\ell\) (up to rank defects of probability about \(2^{\ell-k}\) each), and their total density \((n+1)/2\) is far below the covering threshold \(k\ln2\) of independent flats as soon as \(k\) exceeds a constant times \(n\): the covering is a pigeonhole fact, not a density fact. Through the decoder the bit degree is at least the unary degree, so Conjecture H1 implies \(D_b\ge c\min(n,k/\ell)\); this bit form is what the value method of Claim G uses. No upper relation between the two degrees is recorded, so the bit-degree counts below are not comparable with the unary tipping counts of the two previous entries.

Reading. (1) What the computation can test. The bit form of Conjecture H1, \(D_b\ge c\min(n,k/\ell)\) with \(c\le1/2\), exceeds the unconditional bound \(D_b\ge\ell\) of Lemma R only for \(k>2\ell^2\), that is \(k\ge33\) on sixteen holes and \(k\ge51\) on thirty-two, far beyond the dimensions a closure can reach; and by monotonicity along the chain the tipping points below give \(D_b(W_k)\ge7\) for every \(k\ge17\) on the sixteen-hole chains, which is at least \(\tfrac12\min(n,k/\ell)\) for every \(k\le56\). On eight holes the conjectured bound is at most 4 and the observed degree is the largest possible from \(k=12\) on (from \(k=11\) for seeds 2 and 3). So the conjecture could not have failed on any board within reach: the planned attempt to break it was vacuous, and the conjecture is recorded as not tested. What the data do test is a stronger hypothesis, that \(D_b(W_k)\) stays within two of the generic count until it meets the degree of the full base. (2) Sixteen and thirty-two holes. Every completed scan gives the same largest refuted dimension for the three seeds, and it is the count or one to two below it: 9, 12, 16 against 9, 13, 18, and 11, 15 against 11, 16. The system is never easier than the count in these scans. The degree-seven scans with seed 1 were stopped by hand shortly before their time limit while still refuting (through \(k=17\) on sixteen holes and \(k=18\) on thirty-two; counts 22 and 20); the other seeds were not run at that degree. (3) The control. The bijective control differs from the PHP by one row (120 against 136, and 496 against 528, collision flats of the same kind), so it controls for the pigeonhole principle, not for the collision structure. On these subspaces it is unsatisfiable as well (a brute-force count finds no point with distinct labels for \(k\le18\) on sixteen and thirty-two holes; the first appears at \(k=19\) or 20 on sixteen) and tips at the same dimension or one below, in step with its own count: the pigeonhole principle plays no visible role in the range reached. Independent random flats were not run; the count is the only proxy for them. (4) Four and eight holes, where the structure shows. On eight holes degrees three and four stay within one of the count (7 and 10 to 11 against 7 and 11), and the control becomes satisfiable at \(k=10,7,8\) for the three seeds, which is where its scans stop. The full base is refuted at degree five in the original coordinates, against a count of 15 at that degree, and on four holes at degree three against a count of 9: the full base beats the generic count. With the recorded lower bound \(n/2+1\) for the compact base its bit degree is exactly three on four holes and exactly five on eight, and by monotonicity every subspace is refuted at that degree. On eight holes \(D_b(W_k)\) is at least the minimum of the count and five and within one of it (at \(k=11\) seeds 2 and 3 need degree five where the count gives four). (5) Summary. No refutation below the generic count appeared for \(k\le17\). If the full base has bit degree of order \(n\), as on four and eight holes, and the stronger hypothesis held throughout, the degree at \(k=0.3v\) would be the smaller of about \(0.08\,n\ell\) (the count, with the computed ratio) and the degree of the full base; nothing computed here reaches that regime. Eight holes is already a test of the stronger hypothesis where only the pigeonhole principle makes the system unsatisfiable (item 4); the next such test beyond eight holes: sixteen holes, degree seven, \(k=19\) to 22, with 94,184 to 280,600 monomials, that is dense closures of 1.1 to 9.8 GB and, at the cubic growth observed (six minutes at 41,226 monomials), about one hour at \(k=19\) and about thirty at \(k=22\) with the present tool. The counts are in bit degree and are not comparable with the unary tipping counts of the two previous entries.

(a) Weights supported on \(W\). Corollary SL uses the functional \(\mu(\tau R\,\cdot)\) with \(R\) the indicator of \(W\). A nonzero function on \(\mathbb F_2^v\) that vanishes outside \(W\) has multilinear degree at least \(a\): in the coordinates of \(E\) it is \(\prod_c(1+u_c)\,g(y)\) with \(g\ne0\), whose multilinear form contains \(u_1\cdots u_a\) times the top monomial of \(g\), and an invertible affine map over \(\mathbb F_2\) preserves multilinear degree ( recorded remark ). A polynomial of unary degree \(r\) is, on the labelings, a sum of functions of at most \(r\) labels each, of bit degree at most \(r\ell\). So a weight that vanishes outside \(W\) as a function on the labelings has unary degree at least \(a/\ell\), which for \(a=0.7v\) is \(0.7(n+1)\), above the barrier \(n/2+1\) of the base. This excludes pointwise weights at linear codimension. It does not exclude a weight \(f\) with \(f\Lambda_c\) in the old ideal only through the working degree; no such weight was found. For a single partial-matching monomial \(f=X_T\) with \(|T|<n/2\), \(B\ge|T|+1\) and \(n-|T|\ge2B-1\) the condition holds for all \(c\) exactly if every \(\Lambda_c\) has all its bits in the rows of \(T\) and vanishes at the labels of \(T\) (the restriction that sets \(T\) maps \(X_T\tau\Lambda_c\) to a polynomial of degree at most one on the residual board, the recorded \(\mathcal I_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le1}=\mathcal I_1\) makes it a combination of row axioms, and a nonzero linear functional of the label is not constant on the more than \(n/2\) free holes); this forces \(a\le|T|\ell\) and fails for a generic \(W\).

The bound set by the review is reached: two entries produced Corollary SL (rank up to \(n/4\), a corollary of a recorded detector), the literature position (rank of order \(n\)), Lemma R, two finite checks that do not test the conjecture, and neither a lemma at rank of order \(v\) nor a usable published tool. Conjecture H1 is therefore parked next to Conjecture L , with this record: proved for safe systems of rank up to \(n/4\) at one degree per equation; not tested: on every board within reach its bit form is implied by \(D_b\ge\ell\) and the computed tipping points; the stronger hypothesis that the bit degree stays within two of the generic count up to the degree of the full base holds for \(k\le17\) on sixteen and thirty-two holes and says nothing yet about the regime the conjecture is needed for (\(k\) a constant fraction of \(v\) on large boards); the recorded proof methods fail for the reasons of Section 2. The following entry is a route review that takes up alternative (E) of the last review. Open besides the conjecture itself: whether the full compact base has bit degree of order \(n\) or of order \(n\ell\) (on four and eight holes it is exactly the recorded unary bound \(n/2+1\), three and five), and whether a weight in the weaker sense of Section 2(a) exists.

Image methods stop at the universal obstruction ; the value method needs the PHP to stay hard on a subspace cut out by linear constraints of rank of order \(v\); the union source and the unary parities lead to the same requirement. Every technique on record or read stops at rank of order \(n\): the recorded detectors at \(n/4\), where they reserve holes ( Corollary SL ), the case split at about \(n/2\), where its additive loss meets the barrier, the closure technique for Res(\(\oplus\)) at \(cn\) ( literature ), the expander method at locality. Rank \(n\) is where a system can still be solved for one bit in each of distinct rows; above it every row is touched and all but a \(2^{-t}\) fraction of the linear forms on \(W\) have no representation by bits of \(r\) rows or fewer when \(r\ell+n+1+t\le\dim W\) (there are at most \(\binom{n+1}r2^{r\ell}\) such representations), so an accounting that charges a bounded number of rows to a query stops.

A depth lower bound of order \(n\) for parity decision trees on a generic subspace of linear codimension is therefore a necessary condition for the bit form of the conjecture, and it is the simplest question on which all the techniques above fail for the same reason. For the full space such a bound is published (the abstract of Byramji and Impagliazzo, read in the previous literature entry , states depth \(\Omega(n)\); imported context, not used).

Lemma T (parity decision trees give polynomial-calculus degree). Let \(W\), \(P\) and \(\mathcal S_P\) be as in Lemma R . Suppose a parity decision tree of depth \(d\ge\ell\) solves the collision search on \(W\): every query is a linear form that is not constant on the current subspace, and every leaf, an affine subspace \(U=\{q_1=a_1,\dots,q_s=a_s\}\) of \(W\) with \(s\le d\), lies inside the collision flat of some pair \(p(U)\). Then \(\mathcal S_P\) has a refutation of degree at most \(d\) in the multilinear quotient ring, in fact the Nullstellensatz certificate \(1=\sum_UE_{p(U)}\prod_{j\in J_U}(1+q_j+a_j)\) with \(|J_U|=\operatorname{codim}U-e_{p(U)}\). Hence \(D_b(W)\) is at most the larger of \(\ell\) and the parity-decision-tree depth of the collision search on \(W\), and at most \(\max(\ell,\dim W)\), by querying all coordinates (a point lies in a collision flat because there are more rows than holes).

Position in the record. The recorded case-split lemma gives \(\ell+d\) by induction on the tree (each parity query costs one degree); the bound \(\max(d,\ell)\) without the additive \(\ell\) and the general fact behind it are new. Recorded analogues, none of which implies it: the hole-query trees on the unary board, the branch closure for products of at most three affine forms, and the affine-clause transfers of the publication branch, which go through extension variables. The containment \(R_p\subseteq Q_s\) is the argument of the recorded paragraph on parity decision trees at the end of the unary-query section (a leaf inside a flat of codimension \(r\) has queried rank at least \(r\)). The lemma uses \(\mathbb F_2\) (a linear query is a polynomial of degree one) and nothing about the PHP beyond the axioms being flat indicators; genericity of \(W\) and the non-constancy of the queries (constant queries can be skipped) are not used, and \(d\ge\ell\) only keeps the axiom within the ceiling and gives the passage to \(D_b\) through Lemma R.

Corollary (the compact base has bit degree of order \(n\)). \(n/2+1\le D_b(\mathcal Q_{n,2})\le2n-2+\ell\), and \(D_b(W)\le\min(\max(\ell,\dim W),\,2n-2+\ell)\) for every affine subspace \(W\). The lower bound is the recorded one . For the upper bound use the halving tree: query the first bit of all \(n+1\) rows and keep the \(n/2+1\) rows of the majority side, which share \(n/2\) holes; query the second bit of those rows, and so on; level \(j\) makes \(n/2^{j-1}+1\) queries, \(2n-2+\ell\) in all, and after level \(\ell\) two rows agree in every bit, so the leaf lies in their collision flat. The tree restricted to \(W\) solves the search on \(W\). Image methods stop at the universal obstruction ; the value method needs the PHP to stay hard on a subspace cut out by linear constraints of rank of order \(v\); the union source and the unary parities lead to the same requirement. Every technique on record or read stops at rank of order \(n\): the recorded detectors at \(n/4\), where they reserve holes ( Corollary SL ), the case split at about \(n/2\), where its additive loss meets the barrier, the closure technique for Res(\(\oplus\)) at \(cn\) ( literature ), the expander method at locality. Rank \(n\) is where a system can still be solved for one bit in each of distinct rows; above it every row is touched and all but a \(2^{-t}\) fraction of the linear forms on \(W\) have no representation by bits of \(r\) rows or fewer when \(r\ell+n+1+t\le\dim W\) (there are at most \(\binom{n+1}r2^{r\ell}\) such representations), so an accounting that charges a bounded number of rows to a query stops.

Lemma T (parity decision trees give polynomial-calculus degree). Let \(W\), \(P\) and \(\mathcal S_P\) be as in Lemma R . Suppose a parity decision tree of depth \(d\ge\ell\) solves the collision search on \(W\): every query is a linear form that is not constant on the current subspace, and every leaf, an affine subspace \(U=\{q_1=a_1,\dots,q_s=a_s\}\) of \(W\) with \(s\le d\), lies inside the collision flat of some pair \(p(U)\). Then \(\mathcal S_P\) has a refutation of degree at most \(d\) in the multilinear quotient ring, in fact the Nullstellensatz certificate \(1=\sum_UE_{p(U)}\prod_{j\in J_U}(1+q_j+a_j)\) with \(|J_U|=\operatorname{codim}U-e_{p(U)}\). Hence \(D_b(W)\) is at most the larger of \(\ell\) and the parity-decision-tree depth of the collision search on \(W\), and at most \(\max(\ell,\dim W)\), by querying all coordinates (a point lies in a collision flat because there are more rows than holes).

Position in the record. The recorded case-split lemma gives \(\ell+d\) by induction on the tree (each parity query costs one degree); the bound \(\max(d,\ell)\) without the additive \(\ell\) and the general fact behind it are new. Recorded analogues, none of which implies it: the hole-query trees on the unary board, the branch closure for products of at most three affine forms, and the affine-clause transfers of the publication branch, which go through extension variables. The containment \(R_p\subseteq Q_s\) is the argument of the recorded paragraph on parity decision trees at the end of the unary-query section (a leaf inside a flat of codimension \(r\) has queried rank at least \(r\)). The lemma uses \(\mathbb F_2\) (a linear query is a polynomial of degree one) and nothing about the PHP beyond the axioms being flat indicators; genericity of \(W\) and the non-constancy of the queries (constant queries can be skipped) are not used, and \(d\ge\ell\) only keeps the axiom within the ceiling and gives the passage to \(D_b\) through Lemma R.

Proof. By the recorded observation , except with probability \(\binom{n+1}{r}2^{r\ell-a}\) no two points of \(W\) differ in at most \(r\) rows. A restriction of the compact family fixes every row outside its \(N+1\) live rows to one label, so two assignments that it leaves differ in at most \(N+1\) rows. Take \(r=N+1\); the event does not depend on \(\rho'\), so no union over the family is needed. \(\square\)

For \(a=0.7v\) and polylogarithmic \(N\) the hypothesis holds with room to spare. So on the union source the two recorded mechanisms cannot be combined by intersecting their axioms: whatever restriction serves the reader leaves at most one point of the subspace that serves the twisted source, and on a point the base is refuted at degree at most \(\ell\) (Lemma T below; on an empty intersection at degree one), so hardness is lost outright. The claim itself, which quantifies over all \(E\), is not refuted. With the equations of the twisted source alone, the general form of Lemma R (its Hypotheses paragraph: the substitution acts on the old variables only, with \(\ell\) replaced by the largest axiom degree) puts the whole system into the residual coordinates of \(W\), where every pin \([a\to y]\) of the reader is a flat indicator of codimension at most \(\ell\) in forms that are generic for a generic twist; the reader is then a reader of dense-form terms and falls under the term-value form of Question H . With a restriction alone, the twisted source becomes a reader of generic flats on the polylogarithmic residual space, as in the recorded invariance (which is stated for uniform forms; the rows of a uniform invertible matrix are only approximately uniform). Either way the union source leads back to the same hardness question, on one of the two spaces. Over \(\mathbb F_2\) the distinction between literal and dense terms depends on the coordinates; the hardness question does not.

The line's claim is Claim G (image or value): for a compiled source there are value axioms \(E\), linear equations in the bits or term values, such that the base with \(E\) stays hard and modulo \(E\) every block has an old image. The main goal needs the general step for the sources that short proofs produce, not for generic ones. Two facts from the record fix what that means at the first MOD level. A parity of the variables of the ordinary PHP becomes, in the bit encoding, a sum of arbitrary within-row functions \(a_0+\sum_if_i(b_i)\), a class of dimension \(1+m(n-1)\) against \(1+m\ell\) for affine bit forms ( recorded characterization ); so the simplest gate that an \(\mathrm{AC}^0[2]\)-Frege proof of the ordinary PHP uses is already a sum of low flat indicators, outside the class of the all-ranks one-level theorem . And a two-level source of this kind reduces without degree loss to the one-level unary affine family ( normalization ), for which the record has an inventory on which both recorded rank tests fail ( multiscale family , criterion gap ) and an exclusion at high rank only, with intermediate ranks open ( high-rank coverage ); the all-ranks theorems are for affine-bit families. The record's own caveat stands: the failure of the two tests is not an impossibility theorem, and no proof is known to use the inventory. The generic dense bit forms studied in the last eight entries are therefore a model of the frontier ( stated for bit forms ), not the simplest recorded unexcluded class; the simplest is one OR over parities of PHP variables at middle rank. For both, the value method asks the same thing of the base: hardness under linear constraints of rank far above \(n\), with right-hand sides of our choice. For bit-linear constraints that is Conjecture H1; for parities of unary variables the constraints are \(\sum_if_i(b_i)=e\) with arbitrary \(f_i\), a larger class. Recorded for it: the case split , which covers arbitrary old polynomial queries with right-hand sides of our choice at one degree per query, hence rank up to about \(n/2\), and the occupancy-probe theorem , an example where unary linear equations with the wrong right-hand sides drop the PHP to degree two.

Proof. A fixed nonzero linear form annihilates the direction space of \(W\) with probability \((2^a-1)/(2^v-1)<2^{-k}\), and at most \(\binom{n+1}r2^{r\ell}\) nonzero forms are supported on \(r\) rows or fewer. So except with probability \(2^{-t}\) no nonzero form supported on at most \(r\) rows is constant on \(W\); equivalently, for every set \(S'\) of at most \(r\) rows the projection of \(W\) to the label bits of \(S'\) is onto. This is the event that every set of \(r\) rows has jointly free labels on \(W\), stated without proof in the earlier entry . Note \(r\le k/\ell\le n+1\). Assume the event, fix a tree and an assignment, and suppose that on every path the assigned forms jointly touch at most \(r-2\le n-1\) rows. A delayer walks down the tree and keeps the set \(S\) of rows touched so far and a point \(x\) of the whole bit space that satisfies the answers given so far and is injective on \(S\). At a node with assigned form \(\tilde q\) it adds the rows of \(\tilde q\) to \(S\), changes \(x\) on the new rows to distinct labels not used on the old rows (possible because \(|S|\le n\), and harmless because the earlier forms do not involve the new rows), and answers \(\tilde q(x)\). Let the walk end at a leaf \(U\) with pair \(p\). If a row of \(p\) lies outside \(S\), change \(x\) there so that the two labels of \(p\) differ; otherwise they differ already, because \(x\) is injective on \(S\). As \(|S\cup p|\le r\), some \(w\in W\) agrees with \(x\) on the rows of \(S\cup p\). The assigned forms agree with the queries on \(W\) and are supported on \(S\), so \(w\) gives the delayer's answers and lies in \(U\); but \(w\) does not lie in the collision flat of \(p\). So the tree does not solve the search. (The same argument at an inner node shows that every answer of the delayer is realised on the current subspace of \(W\), so the walk never enters an empty branch.) \(\square\)

For \(k=0.3v\) the condition reads \(r\le0.3(n+1)-(\log_2\binom{n+1}r+t)/\ell\), which allows \(r\) about \((0.3-0.88/\ell)n\), at least \(0.3n-n/\ell\): vacuous for \(\ell\le4\) (at \(\ell=4\) the condition allows \(r=2\) only), about two rows at \(\ell=5\), and a fraction of \(n\) that tends to \(0.3\) as \(\ell\) grows. So on a generic subspace of codimension \(0.7v\) every tree whose queries touch at most \(\omega\) rows each has depth more than \((r-2)/\omega\): ordinary decision trees on the bits need depth of order \(n\). This is the standard adversary argument, run on \(W\) through the free rows; it is a bound at rank of order \(v\), but only for the weakest kind of query. A prover that does better must use queries that touch many rows in every representation; all but a \(2^{-t}\) fraction of the forms on \(W\) are of this kind ( counting sentence of the review ). I found no strategy that uses such queries (two wide queries whose sum is a pair form give one narrow form for two queries, and are available on the whole space as well), and no proof that none exists. The attempt to build a prover of depth \(o(n)\) ends here.

Use on the whole space. Let \(W\) be the whole bit space and \(G=G^{[j]}\) be the points whose \(n+1\) labels take exactly \(n+1-j\) values (\(j=1\): one colliding pair), and \(\bar c_j\) the average number of colliding pairs of a point of \(G\). All pairs are equivalent, so \(|G\cap F_p|=\bar c_j|G|/\binom{n+1}2\), and the density of \(G\) inside a collision flat is smaller than in the whole space by the factor \(\beta_j=(n+1)/(2\bar c_j)\). Inside the flat of \(p\), with the two rows of \(p\) merged, \(G\cap F_p\) is the set \(S_{j-1}\) of labelings of \(n\) rows by \(n\) labels with image size \(n-j+1\). So on the full space a tree of depth \(d\) exists only if some affine subspace of codimension at most \(d-\ell\) of \(\mathbb F_2^{n\ell}\) carries \(S_{j-1}\) at density at least \(\beta_j\) times its average, a density boost \(\beta_j\). The depth is thus at least \(\ell\) plus the least codimension at which near-injective labelings can be concentrated by the factor \(\beta_j\) on an affine subspace. For an affine subspace \(H\) with annihilator \(A\) (a space of characters, \(|A|=2^s\)) the boost is \(\sum_{\chi\in A}\pm\hat S(\chi)/\hat S(0)\), at most \(1\) plus the sum of the \(2^s-1\) largest values of \(|\hat S(\chi)|/\hat S(0)\), \(\chi\ne0\) (the spectral bound of the table below), hence at most \(1+(2^s-1)\max_{\chi\ne0}|\hat S(\chi)|/\hat S(0)\). On a generic \(W\) the factor \(\beta_j\) holds only on average over the pairs, and the identification with \(S_{j-1}\) is not available; Lemma D itself holds for every \(W\) and every \(G\). The record already gives a depth bound on the whole space by another route: by Lemma T the depth is at least the bit degree, which is at least \(n/2+1\) ( recorded ); the interest of Lemma D is its use on \(W\), where the bit degree is unknown.

Question A (concentration of near-injective labelings). For \(j\ge2\) fixed, what is the least codimension \(s_j(n)\) of an affine subspace of \(\mathbb F_2^{n\ell}\) on which \(S_{j-1}\) has density \(\beta_j\) times its average? The needed boost is not a constant: \(\beta_2=(n+1)(3n-2)/(12n)\), about \(n/4\). An upper bound, the birthday subspace. Prescribe distinct \(t\)-bit prefixes on \(m\le2^t\) rows: codimension \(mt\). Under a uniform bijection the labels of the \(m\) rows are a uniform injective tuple, so the subspace has probability \(\prod_{i<m}(n/2^t)/(n-i)\) against \(2^{-tm}\) under the uniform measure: boost \(n^m(n-m)!/n!\), which is \(\exp(m^2/(2n)+O(m^3/n^2))\). For \(S_1\) the labels of the \(m\) rows are a uniform injective tuple given that the colliding pair does not lie inside them, so the boost is \(\bigl(1-\binom m2/\binom n2\bigr)n^m(n-m)!/n!\). It exceeds \(\beta_2\) at \(m\) about \(\sqrt{2n\ln(n/4)}\), codimension \(m\lceil\log_2m\rceil\) (or \(m(\lceil\log_2m\rceil-1)+1\), prescribing only the pair conditions of the prefix tree, which changes the constant only): 742 for \(n=2^{10}\), 5200 for \(n=2^{14}\) (below \(n/2+1=8193\)), 66456 for \(n=2^{20}\). Balanced halving is much weaker: fixing the first bit on \(m\) rows, half each way, boosts bijections by \([2^m/\binom m{m/2}]\binom{n/2}{m/2}^2/\binom nm\), about \((1-m/n)^{-1/2}\) for \(m<n\) and \(\sqrt{\pi n/2}\) at \(m=n\). The birthday characters are visible in the spectrum: the second coefficient \(0.102\) of \(S_1\) on eight holes belongs to the characters \((-1)^{\langle z,\mathrm{label}_i+\mathrm{label}_{i'}\rangle}\) of two rows, with value \(\frac1{28}-\frac{27}{28}\cdot\frac17=-20/196\). Consequence. With \(G^{[2]}\) Lemma D cannot prove more than depth \(O(\ell\sqrt{n\log n})\) on the whole space, where the record gives \(n/2+1\): the density criterion loses at least a square root there, and the same subspace limits \(G^{[j]}\) for other fixed \(j\) (not computed). Compare with the working degree of the recorded framework, \(B=k(D+1)\) with \(k\) of order \(\sqrt{n\log M}\) ( review ): the ceiling is of the same order up to logarithmic factors, so through \(G^{[2]}\) Lemma D can at best match the working degree, and even a complete answer to Question A with the transfer would not exclude provers of depth between about \(\ell\sqrt{n\log n}\) and \(B\); a depth bound is in any case only a necessary condition for degree hardness. So \(s_2(n)\) lies between about \(2\ell-2\) (spectral bound, given the largest coefficient) and \(O(\ell\sqrt{n\log n})\). The transfer to a generic \(W\) is the part that concerns the wall: one needs that on \(W\) no subspace concentrates \(G^{[j]}\cap W\) more than the subspaces of the whole space do. I tried the moment method and it does not reach this (an account of a failed attempt, not a claim): for one fixed subspace \(H\) of the whole space the second moment shows that \(W\cap H\cap G\) has about the expected size as long as \(k-\operatorname{codim}H\) exceeds \(\log_2(2^v/|G|)\), about \(1.44n\) for small \(j\); but there are about \(2^{sv}\) subspaces \(H\) of codimension \(s\), so a union bound over them needs failure probabilities below \(2^{-sv}\), and in the higher moments that I computed the events that the parameter subspace of \(W\) falls into a structured \(H\) dominate once \(s\) exceeds about \(\ell/2\). So after this entry the delayer side has a criterion (Lemma D), its first obstruction (the linear invariant of bijections, avoided by \(j\ge2\)), a logarithmic bound from spectra, a ceiling of order \(\ell\sqrt{n\log n}\) from the birthday subspace (no higher than the working degree of the value method, up to logarithmic factors), and two open statements: Question A on the whole space and the transfer. Second and last entry: decide whether the boost of \(S_1\) at codimension \(s\) is at most \(\exp(O(s^2/n))\), which is what the birthday subspace suggests and would give \(s_2(n)\) of order at least \(\sqrt{n\log n}\) (sequential argument: reveal the rows one at a time; row \(i\) is uniform on a flat whose shift is an affine function of the earlier rows), and whether the transfer holds with the maximum over \(H\) in place of each \(H\).

Lemma N (sequential boost bound). (a) For \(S\) the injective labelings of \(\rho\le n\) rows, \(\mathrm{boost}(H)\le\prod_{i\ \mathrm{pivot}}\frac n{n-i+1}\le\frac{n^\tau(n-\tau)!}{n!}\) for every ordering of \(T\), with equality on the birthday subspace of the previous entry. (b) For \(S=S_1\), the labelings of \(n\) rows with exactly one colliding pair, \(\mathrm{boost}(H)\le\prod_{i\ \mathrm{pivot}}\frac{n+3}{n-i+1}\) for every ordering of \(T\) (the proof gives \(n+2\)).

What the lemma gives and what it does not. The bound depends on the rows touched, not on the codimension: with \(\tau\) rows the boost of \(S_1\) is at most \((1+3/n)^\tau n^\tau(n-\tau)!/n!\), about \(\exp(\tau^2/2n)\), so the birthday subspace is optimal among subspaces defined on few rows, and a boost \(\beta_2\approx n/4\) needs \(\tau\) at least about \(\sqrt{2n\ln(n/4)}\) rows. For forms of large row width the bound says nothing, and for bijections it cannot: the sum-zero subspace has boost \(n\) at codimension \(\ell\), every ordering has a pivot at the last position with ratio \(n\), and (a) is attained there as well. In the application of Lemma D the subspace lives inside a collision flat on the \(n\) merged entities, \(T\) counts entities, and a query that touches a row of the pair touches the merged entity. There the lemma gives depth at least \(\ell\) plus about \(\sqrt{2n\ln(n/4)}/\omega\) on the whole space for queries of row width \(\omega\), which is weaker than the injective-point adversary of Lemma L (order \(n/\omega\)). So Lemma N adds no depth bound; it shows that Question A is entirely a question about forms of large row width, the same place where the prover side stopped.

Absolute values lose the signs. The boost is a signed sum of normalised coefficients over the characters of \(A\), and the spectral bound of the previous entry replaces it by the sum of absolute values. Take \(H\) the subspace that fixes the labels of \(m\) rows to distinct values (\(s=m\ell\)). For bijections the character that applies one functional \(z\ne0\) to two rows has coefficient exactly \(-1/(n-1)\) (the sum of two distinct uniform labels is uniform on the nonzero vectors), and \(A\) contains \((n-1)\binom m2\) of them: absolute sum \(\binom m2\), signed sum \(\binom m2/(n-1)\) (for each pair, \(\sum_{z\ne0}-(-1)^{\langle z,a_i+a_{i'}\rangle}/(n-1)=1/(n-1)\)), which is the first-order term of the true \(\ln\) boost \(m^2/2n\). Likewise for \(S_1\), where the two-row coefficient is \(1/\binom n2-(1-1/\binom n2)/(n-1)\), about \(-(1-3/n)/n\) ( previous entry ), and the absolute sum is \(\binom m2(1-O(1/n))\). So no argument through absolute values can show a boost below \(1+\binom m2\) at codimension \(m\ell\), that is, it cannot answer Question A beyond codimension about \(\ell\sqrt{n/2}\); counting also the characters on \(j\) disjoint pairs (about \((m^2/2)^j(n-1)^j/j!\) of them with coefficients about \(n^{-j}\); heuristic, not proved) the absolute sum is about \(\exp(m^2/2)\) and the method stops near \(1.2\,\ell^{3/2}\), barely above the \(2\ell-2\) of the spectra.

The transfer, reformulated. The account in the previous entry counted the \(2^{sv}\) subspaces of codimension \(s\); the better count is over characters. Let \(W=c+W_0\) with \(W_0\) a uniform subspace of dimension \(k\) and \(c\) uniform, \(G\) a point set and \(f(\varphi)=|G|^{-1}\sum_{x\in G}\varphi(x)\). Expanding the indicator of \(W\) gives, for every character \(\chi\), \(\sum_{x\in G\cap W}\chi(x)=2^{-a}|G|\sum_{\psi\in W_0^\perp}\psi(c)f(\chi\psi)\): the coefficient of \(G\cap W\) at the class of \(\chi\) is \(f(\chi)\) plus the noise \(N(\chi)=\sum_{\psi\ne0}\psi(c)f(\chi\psi)\), normalised by \(1+N(1)\). The average over \(c\) gives \(\mathbb E N(\chi)=0\) and \(\mathbb E N(\chi)^2=\sum_{\psi\ne0}\Pr[\psi\in W_0^\perp]f(\chi\psi)^2<2^{-k}2^v/|G|\) by Parseval, about \(2^{-k+1.44n}\) for \(G^{[2]}\). This controls one character, not all \(2^v\) of them; a simultaneous bound needs moments of order above \(v/(k/2-0.72n)\), in which the average over \(c\) leaves the tuples of characters with trivial product, and the characters with large coefficients (small row width, and their products with the uniform characters) have to be separated as main terms, which is where the free-rows event of Lemma L would enter. I did not carry this out: its outcome would be that the coefficients of \(G\cap W\) are those of \(G\) up to a small error, after which the transfer inherits exactly the problem of the whole space, signed sums over characters of large row width.

A closed form for one functional on \(w\) rows. For bijections the character that applies one functional \(z\ne0\) to \(w\) rows has coefficient \((-1)^{w/2}\binom{n/2}{w/2}/\binom nw\) for even \(w\) and zero for odd \(w\): the labels of the \(w\) rows form a uniform \(w\)-subset of the labels, half of which satisfy \(\langle z,x\rangle=1\), and \(\sum_j(-1)^j\binom{n/2}j\binom{n/2}{w-j}\) is the coefficient of \(x^w\) in \((1-x^2)^{n/2}\). It gives \(-1/7\) at \(w=2\) and \(w=6\) on eight holes, as in the computed spectrum , and about \(2^{-n/2}\) at \(w=n/2\): single characters of middle width are negligible, and only a subspace with very many of them, with aligned signs, could matter.

Thesis. Every form of the general step that has produced a polynomial-calculus exclusion at a degree not tied to the accuracy of the blocks is of one type: a design of an enlarged old base \(\mathcal F\cup E\) composed with old images of the blocks modulo \(E\). The forms differ only in \(E\): a weight \(w\) (over \(\mathbb F_2\), for \(\mathcal F\) containing the Boolean equations and \(\deg w\le B\), \(w\notin\mathcal C_{B+\deg w}(\mathcal F)\) implies that \(\mathcal F\cup\{1+w\}\) has no refutation of degree \(B\), which implies \(w\notin\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F)\); so the one-affine-level theorem , the learning lemma and the relative interfaces are of this type with \(E=\{1+w\}\)), matching restrictions (the literal line, Conjecture L ), linear value axioms and term values ( Claim G , the reduction ). Each needs a hardness statement \(H(E)\) about the old base alone, and the proof techniques on record for \(H(E)\) are four: counting a common weight, restrictions that preserve the base, the top-monomial detectors (rank at most \(n/4\), Corollary SL ), and the case split (additive loss). The standing reviewer, asked for recorded forms outside this type, named three, with their recorded status: (a) source-module moment designs, in which the selector moments are free unknowns ( coupled marginals , active-window reduction , pair-separated transfer ): this form does have unconditional Nullstellensatz extensions with no charge for the number of blocks or their rank, but only in the band \(3h<D\le4h\) tied to the accuracy and for bit-affine families ( first boundary , coherent band , faithful pairs ), coverage at rank at most \(4h\) in the band \(6h\le D<8h\) ( corollary ), no feasibility theorem beyond, and three recorded obstructions to simple ansätze (statuses from the index rows; these entries were not re-read for this review); (b) fresh-block conservativity through the coefficient criterion and its dual: open at level one ( conjecture ), refuted at the same degree over second-level bases, with loss at most \(\min(D+k\delta,2D-w)\) per block ( loss bound ) and total rank under sequential application ( placement ); (c) proof-specific forms, in which \(E\) is chosen after the refutation is given: escapes are named ( obstruction entry , published extension-variable methods ), local pruning exists, and no theorem uses the structure of the source of a short proof. The generic query route is parked by its own obstruction .

Lemma K (constant-row clamp). Work over \(\mathbb F_p\). Let a source over an old base \(\mathcal F\) have complete first-level blocks \(b\le M\) with old inputs \(g_{b,1},\dots,g_{b,r_b}\) and accuracies \(h_b\), \(P_b=\prod_{u\le h_b}(1-\sum_jr_{b,u,j}g_{b,j})\). Choose constants \(c_{b,u,j}\) and put \(\lambda_{b,u}=\sum_jc_{b,u,j}g_{b,j}\), \(Q_b=\prod_{u\le h_b}(1-\lambda_{b,u})\). (i) If \(\mathcal F\cup\{g_{b,i}Q_b:b,i\}\) has no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree \(D\), then \(\mathcal F\) with the blocks has none. (ii) Over \(\mathbb F_2\): if the source has, above the first level, only pure readers in the sense of the recorded reduction , and \(\mathcal F\cup\{Q_b:b\le M\}\) has no refutation of degree \(D\), then the source has none of degree \(D\).

Scope, as the reviewer pointed out. Part (i) uses nothing about \(\mathcal F\); (ii) and the remarks (b), (c) below are written for \(\mathbb F_2\) (for odd \(p\) the reader cases select an input congruent to \(c\ne0\) with \(c^{-1}\), and flat indicators need powers \(p-1\); not written out). The lemma is not in the record in this form; the nearest records are the constant first-row specialization at the end of the learning lemma, the zeroing of surplus rows in the relative old-target theorem , and the recorded reduction with its nonconstant telescoping images. (a) Part (ii) needs the stronger axioms \(Q_b\); with \(g_{b,i}Q_b\) alone the product is not constant, the axioms only exclude the flat of \(\lambda\) minus the zero set \(Z_b\) of the block. (b) Since \(Z_b=Z_bQ_b\) modulo Booleanity, hardness of \(\mathcal F\cup\{Q_b\}\) at \(B+h\) implies hardness of \(\mathcal F\cup\{Z_b\}\) at \(B\): the hypothesis of (ii) is stronger than the zero-value hypothesis of the recorded reduction, and what it buys is the removal of the factor \(w-1\) at every rank above \(h\). It is Question H at rank \(h\) with total density \(M2^{-h}\). (c) For a block of rank at most \(h\), taking the \(\lambda_u\) a basis makes the companions Boolean consequences; this is the recorded packing. Each needs a hardness statement \(H(E)\) about the old base alone, and the proof techniques on record for \(H(E)\) are four: counting a common weight, restrictions that preserve the base, the top-monomial detectors (rank at most \(n/4\), Corollary SL ), and the case split (additive loss). The standing reviewer, asked for recorded forms outside this type, named three, with their recorded status: (a) source-module moment designs, in which the selector moments are free unknowns ( coupled marginals , active-window reduction , pair-separated transfer ): this form does have unconditional Nullstellensatz extensions with no charge for the number of blocks or their rank, but only in the band \(3h<D\le4h\) tied to the accuracy and for bit-affine families ( first boundary , coherent band , faithful pairs ), coverage at rank at most \(4h\) in the band \(6h\le D<8h\) ( corollary ), no feasibility theorem beyond, and three recorded obstructions to simple ansätze (statuses from the index rows; these entries were not re-read for this review); (b) fresh-block conservativity through the coefficient criterion and its dual: open at level one ( conjecture ), refuted at the same degree over second-level bases, with loss at most \(\min(D+k\delta,2D-w)\) per block ( loss bound ) and total rank under sequential application ( placement ); (c) proof-specific forms, in which \(E\) is chosen after the refutation is given: escapes are named ( obstruction entry , published extension-variable methods ), local pruning exists, and no theorem uses the structure of the source of a short proof. The generic query route is parked by its own obstruction .

Proof. Substitute \(r_{b,u,j}=c_{b,u,j}\); this is the degree-zero case of the substitution rule . The product \(P_b\) maps to \(Q_b\), each companion \(g_{b,i}P_b\) to \(g_{b,i}Q_b\), each coefficient field equation to \(c^p-c=0\), and old axioms to themselves; no degree changes. This proves (i). For (ii), modulo the axioms \(Q_b\) every first-level product is congruent to 0, so every input of a reader is congruent to a constant, and the two cases of the recorded reduction give the reader a constant image with constant coefficient rows (an input congruent to 1 is selected by the first row, image congruent to 0; if all inputs are congruent to 0 the zero rows give the image 1), and the same one level up. All images use constants, so the factor \(\max(1,w-1)\) of that reduction does not occur. \(\square\)

Scope, as the reviewer pointed out. Part (i) uses nothing about \(\mathcal F\); (ii) and the remarks (b), (c) below are written for \(\mathbb F_2\) (for odd \(p\) the reader cases select an input congruent to \(c\ne0\) with \(c^{-1}\), and flat indicators need powers \(p-1\); not written out). The lemma is not in the record in this form; the nearest records are the constant first-row specialization at the end of the learning lemma, the zeroing of surplus rows in the relative old-target theorem , and the recorded reduction with its nonconstant telescoping images. (a) Part (ii) needs the stronger axioms \(Q_b\); with \(g_{b,i}Q_b\) alone the product is not constant, the axioms only exclude the flat of \(\lambda\) minus the zero set \(Z_b\) of the block. (b) Since \(Z_b=Z_bQ_b\) modulo Booleanity, hardness of \(\mathcal F\cup\{Q_b\}\) at \(B+h\) implies hardness of \(\mathcal F\cup\{Z_b\}\) at \(B\): the hypothesis of (ii) is stronger than the zero-value hypothesis of the recorded reduction, and what it buys is the removal of the factor \(w-1\) at every rank above \(h\). It is Question H at rank \(h\) with total density \(M2^{-h}\). (c) For a block of rank at most \(h\), taking the \(\lambda_u\) a basis makes the companions Boolean consequences; this is the recorded packing. So for first-level blocks the accuracy is the width of the avoidance axiom the block needs , whatever its rank, and the choice of the \(\lambda\) is ours.

The simplest recorded unexcluded class is one OR over parities of PHP variables: the one-level unary affine family over \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) ( Section 2 of the previous review ; in the bit base it is the two-level class with second-level inputs that are sums of low flat indicators, and the normalization returns to the unary family). A superquasipolynomial \(\mathrm{AC}^0[2]\)-Frege lower bound for the ordinary PHP would have to cover proofs that use such gates (the translation of such a proof into this source is the recorded telescoping substitution, a sketch and not a formal implication). The one-affine-level theorem does not cover it (its blocks are affine in the bits). What the record has, with the further items the reviewer listed: exact packing up to rank about \(hN/(2D)\) (ceiling \(T(r)D\)); the dimension criterion at rank at least \(\rho v\), \(v=N(N+1)\), and more generally where \(M\,b_k(v-r)<u_k-t_k\) for some \(k\le N/(2D)\); old-target NS exclusions for jointly independent middle-rank groups on eleven and thirteen holes only (pair-separated transfer); the degree gap of the common-vanishing method for \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1\) independent blocks; and the failure of a unary weight by the ambient dimension. My first formulation of the uncovered window, \(hN/(2D)<r<2D(N+1)\ln(4M)\), was corrected by the reviewer at its upper edge: in the recorded criterion the matching monomials are only a fraction of about \(e^{-k^2/N}\) of \(b_k(v)\) (and the term \(t_k\) makes the criterion vacuous once \(e^{-k^2/N}<k/N\)), so the requirement is about \(r>v\ln(4M)/k+(N+1)k\), smallest near \(k=\sqrt{N\ln4M}\), and the upper edge is about \(2(N+1)\sqrt{N\ln4M}\) once \(N\) exceeds about \(4D^2\ln4M\) (computed by the reviewer for three parameter sets; not gated further). The qualitative statement is the recorded one: ranks around \(N\) lie inside the window on every usable board ( criterion gap ), and the multiscale family has a class there.

Remark (few blocks are conservative in the stable range; a corollary of two records). Over \(\mathbb F_2\), let \(N\ge2B-1\), and adjoin to \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) fresh complete blocks \(1,\dots,M\) whose inputs are old polynomials of degree at most \(\delta\), of any rank and accuracy. If an old polynomial \(t\) of degree \(k\) has a polynomial-calculus derivation of degree \(d\) from the enlarged system and \(d+M\max(\delta,k)\le B\), then \(t\in\mathcal I_k(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun})\). Proof: eliminate the blocks one at a time by the transfer lemma , whose base may contain the other blocks, at the cost \(\max\{d+\delta,d+k,2k\}\) each; the result is a derivation from \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) within \(B\), and \(\mathcal C_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=\mathcal I_k\) brings \(t\) down to its own degree. \(\square\) So the difficulty of the simplest class lies only in the number of blocks: whatever their ranks, \(M\) blocks give no refutation and no old consequence of degree \(k\) while \(d+M\max(\delta,k)\le(N+1)/2\).

This is Question H at rank \(h\) in the unary base, in the regime of small total density, with no substitution factor. There is no finite evidence in the regime itself: the recorded check of the same entry has \(h=2\), where \(M2^{-h}<1\) allows three axioms. What it shows at larger density: on six holes at degree three, with general unary forms, the closure grows by the constant increment 34 per clause of two parities until 1 enters at axiom 50; on eight holes, with decoded bit-affine forms, by 62 until a jump at axiom 91, with 28 percent of the quotient left, and 1 enters at axiom 96 (\(M2^{-h}=24\)). The jump is a cancellation effect of polynomial calculus, which a Nullstellensatz design does not see. No recorded technique proves it: the weight fails by the ambient dimension, restrictions do not act on dense forms, and the case split pays per block.

(1) Do term values weaken the wall on the twisted approximate-majority source? In the test of Claim G the value axioms were the \(0.7v\) linear equations \(u_i=0\), \(i\in I\), and that entry records that every term then lies in their ideal, so hardness with those equations gives the zero-value hypothesis \(E'=\{Z_c=0\text{ for every term }c\}\). Conversely \(E'\) is a weaker sufficient hypothesis, so the sentence there that the claim escapes "exactly if" the PHP stays hard on a generic subspace of codimension \(0.7v\) holds for that \(E\) only. Does \(E'\) avoid linear codimension? The points on which every (positive) term vanishes are the union of the coordinate subspaces \(\{u_S=0\}\) over the hitting sets \(S\) of the terms. For the recorded parameters (\(v\) DNFs of \(\lceil4v(3/2)^t\rceil\) terms, \(t=\lceil3\log_2v\rceil\) uniform coordinates each) a set of density \(\sigma\) misses a given term with probability \((1-\sigma)^t\); the expected number of missed terms is at least \(4v^{2}(1.5(1-\sigma))^t\), which exceeds \(v\) by a power of \(v\) exactly when \(\sigma<1-2^{-1/3}/1.5=0.4709\) (at \(\sigma=0.47\) it is at least \(3.2\,v^{1.007}\)), and a union bound over the sets of size \(\lfloor0.47v\rfloor\) suffices because supersets of hitting sets are hitting sets (failure probability at most \(0.09^v\), reviewer's arithmetic). So with high probability every hitting set has more than \(0.47v\) elements, a sharpening of the \(v/3\) that the approximate-majority property gives by itself. Every point allowed by \(E'\) lies on a coordinate subspace of codimension above \(0.47v\), a generic subspace after the twist. Random sets are hitting sets from density about \(0.58\) (equivalently, a complement fixed beforehand may have density up to about \(0.42\); reviewer). The only recorded route to hardness with \(E'\) is one such subspace, so term values move the instance of Conjecture H1 from dimension \(0.3v\) to at most about \(0.53v\): the wall stays. The source has many narrow terms of total density about \(4v^{0.75}\gg1\); this is the opposite regime to (HW).
